summary: Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Kansas (~1975–1983). She held positions at Kansas, several museums, Hakuho Women's College, and served as professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2007–2019).

Patricia Sauthoff is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She was a PhD candidate at the University of London (attested 2016–2018), taught at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (2016), and was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Alberta (2019–2023) and Hong Kong Baptist University.

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a scholar in sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.
Patrick Marlow is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1997, studying under Hans Henrich Hock.

Patrick McAllister works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser (~2005–2011) and held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, becoming Senior Academy Scientist in 2022.

Patrick McCartney is a researcher in Indology and religious studies. His appointments include a JSPS postdoctoral fellowship at Kyoto University (attested 2018), affiliations at ANU, Nanzan University, and OICD (all attested 2020), and a Phoenix Fellowship at Hiroshima University (attested 2025).

Patrick Olivelle specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Oxford (BA, ~1969–1972) and earned his PhD under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1974). He taught at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 1991).

Patrick Pranke is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued his doctoral studies at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012) under Robert E. Buswell Jr.
Patrick Robert Cadell (1871–1961) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the East India Company College and Balliol College, Oxford (~1890–1891).
Patrick Tugwell is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who has been a graduate and doctoral student at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a Tibetan figure in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under numerous masters, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1830–1843) and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught prominent disciples such as Shenphen Nangwa and Minyak Kunzang Sonam.
Paul Althaus (1888–1966) was a German religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1907–1910) and held an academic post at the University of Rostock (~1920–1925).

Paul Arnold Irzel (1861–1931) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Strasbourg and Munich, and completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig (~1886–1890) under Ernst Windisch.

Paul B. Courtright is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He held an appointment at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and served at Emory University (attested 1996–1998), where he is Professor Emeritus (attested 2026).

Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa (attested 1997) along with several traditional teachers, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After earning a PhD at Tübingen (~1874–1876), he founded the Open Court Publishing Company and edited The Open Court and The Monist (~1887/1890–1919).

Paul Copp is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at UMass Amherst and Princeton (PhD attested 2005) under Stephen F. Teiser, later holding positions at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago.

Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Calgary (1990–1992) and a PhD at the University of British Columbia (1999–2005), joining Simon Fraser University as an associate professor in 2005.

Paul Dahlke (1865–1928) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied in 1900 under Hikkaduwe Sri Sumangala Thera, Ñāṇissara Thera, and W. D. C. Wagiswara, and founded Das Buddhistische Haus in 1924.
